promoted_to_rules.label: Identity Becomes a Border
promoted_to_rules.thesis: Where a population's identity -- language, tribe or region -- does not match the administration governing it, mobilisation follows and the map is eventually redrawn to fit. Language is the paradigm case (Tamil Nadu, Gujarat); tribal identity does the same work in Jharkhand.
promoted_to_rules.game_rule: Governing a population whose language or identity you do not share adds +1 Unrest/turn, compounding. At 10 the territory secedes into a new state — playable by another player in multiplayer.

stages.title: Madras State is renamed Tamil Nadu

promoted_to_rules.label: The Revenue Ratchet
promoted_to_rules.thesis: A revenue demand fixed independently of the harvest converts a bad monsoon into a mass death event. The famine is fiscal, not meteorological.
promoted_to_rules.game_rule: Setting Revenue to Fixed grants +2 Treasury per turn but removes the harvest-failure buffer. A drought while Fixed triggers Famine: -30% population, -2 Legitimacy, permanent Unrest scar.

stages.title: The Company obtains the Diwani of Bengal

local_patterns.label: Insurgency and Accord
local_patterns.thesis: Armed movements in India end at negotiated accords, not at military victory — and unimplemented accords restart the cycle.
local_patterns.game_rule: Insurgency cannot be reduced below 3 by military action. Only Accord clears it — and an Accord whose terms you fail to fund re-ignites at +2 within 10 turns.

stages.title: Operation Blue Star and its aftermath

local_patterns.label: The Long Dividend
local_patterns.thesis: Land reform and schooling pay nothing for a generation, then compound. States that spend early on people outperform states that spend early on plant.
local_patterns.game_rule: Human-capital spend returns nothing for 15 turns, then pays 3x indefinitely. The AI opponents never build it. It is how a resource-poor state wins a long game.

local_patterns.label: The Resource Curse
local_patterns.thesis: Mineral wealth under communally-held land produces extraction, displacement and eventually armed resistance — the insurgency maps onto the ore body.
local_patterns.game_rule: Every Mine placed on tribal-tenure land adds +3 Treasury and +1 permanent Unrest. Unrest above 7 spawns an insurgency that closes the district to all further building until resolved by Accord or Autonomy — never by force alone.

local_patterns.label: The Unmaking of a Craft
local_patterns.thesis: Craft economies die from demand-side policy — monopsony, tariffs, mechanised imports — far faster than from any loss of skill.
local_patterns.game_rule: Artisanry decays 4%/turn while a foreign power holds your Trade channel. Below 25% the craft is LOST — it cannot be rebuilt this era, only revived later at triple cost via a GI-tag project.

local_patterns.label: The Irrigation Trap
local_patterns.thesis: Subsidised water and guaranteed procurement raise yields spectacularly, then lock the region into the crop that exhausts its water.
local_patterns.game_rule: Irrigation gives +50% yield and sets a hidden Water Table counter draining each turn. At zero, yields fall below the pre-irrigation baseline and the fix costs more than the original works.

stages.title: Groundwater depletion and the paddy trap

local_patterns.label: The Cut
local_patterns.thesis: A border drawn through a functioning economy severs producers from markets and people from land; the demographic shock outlives the political one by generations.
local_patterns.game_rule: Partition is the only irreversible map event. You lose territory, gain refugees (Labour +, Housing -, Unrest +), and every adjacency bonus through the severed border is deleted permanently.

local_patterns.label: The Remittance Engine
local_patterns.thesis: Educate a population a poor economy cannot employ and it exports labour; the wages come home as consumption and human development without industrialisation.
local_patterns.game_rule: High Literacy + low Industry opens the Migration channel: -Labour, +Treasury, +Wellbeing, and a hidden Fragility counter tied to a foreign economy you do not control.

local_patterns.label: The Capital Drain
local_patterns.thesis: Losing capital status costs a city more than the buildings it keeps: investment follows administration, and the decline shows up decades later.
local_patterns.game_rule: Moving your capital gives the new city +40% growth and the old one -20% for 20 turns. Reversing the move does not restore it.

stages.title: The capital moves from Calcutta to Delhi

local_patterns.label: Loot into Stone
local_patterns.thesis: Successful conquest is converted into monumental building and endowed craft — the temple is a war memorial with an economy attached.
local_patterns.game_rule: Spending war spoils on a Monument converts one-off Treasury into permanent Legitimacy and unlocks that era's craft tree. Hoarding the spoils instead keeps the gold and forfeits the tree.

local_patterns.label: Harbour to Workshop
local_patterns.thesis: A usable harbour pulls in trade, trade capitalises craft, and craft becomes the region's identity long after the trade moves on.
local_patterns.game_rule: Building a port on a coastal state raises Trade for 3 turns; if Trade stays high for 5 turns, Artisanry gains a permanent +1 craft slot.
